Flag iSNVs with replicate discordance

Source: R/qc-replicate.R
flagReplicateDiscordance.Rd

Identifies variant sites where technical replicates disagree and flags them in the qcPass assay.

Usage

flagReplicateDiscordance(whe, freqTolerance = 0.05, requireBothDetected = TRUE)

Arguments

whe

A WithinHostExperiment with replicate_group and replicate_id columns in colData.

freqTolerance

Numeric scalar. Maximum allowable difference in altFreq between replicates (default: 0.05).

requireBothDetected

Logical scalar. If TRUE (default), sites detected in only one replicate are also flagged. A freqTolerance of 1 or more with requireBothDetected = FALSE would flag nothing, since frequencies lie in [0, 1], and is an error, as it is for a ConcordanceRule.

Value

A WithinHostExperiment with updated qcPass and qcLog.

Details

For each replicate group, the function compares altFreq between replicates and flags sites where the difference exceeds freqTolerance; a difference equal to it, to within rounding error, passes. Sites are flagged in ALL samples of the replicate group.

Roder et al. (2023) reported that the choice of variant caller and the use of replicate sequencing had the largest effects on single-nucleotide variant discovery. An alternative approach is replicate intersection (requiring detection in both replicates); use requireBothDetected = TRUE with freqTolerance = Inf to achieve this.

References

Roder AE et al. (2023). Optimized quantification of intra-host viral diversity in SARS-CoV-2 and influenza virus sequence data. mBio 14:e01046-23. doi:10.1128/mbio.01046-23

See also

flagISNV for standard QC filtering.

Examples

rep1 <- system.file("extdata", "test_donor_rep1.vcf",
    package = "WithinHostExperiment")
rep2 <- system.file("extdata", "test_donor_rep2.vcf",
    package = "WithinHostExperiment")
whe <- readWithinHost(c(rep1, rep2),
    colData = S4Vectors::DataFrame(
        sample_id = c("rep1", "rep2"),
        replicate_group = c("donor_reps", "donor_reps"),
        replicate_id = c("1", "2")),
    caller = "ivar")
whe <- flagReplicateDiscordance(whe, freqTolerance = 0.05)
qcLog(whe)
#> DataFrame with 2 rows and 6 columns
#>                    step           parameter       value n_flagged  n_passed
#>             <character>         <character> <character> <integer> <integer>
#> 1 replicate_discordance       freqTolerance        0.05         6        26
#> 2 replicate_discordance requireBothDetected        TRUE         0        26
#>             timestamp
#>           <character>
#> 1 2026-11-26T12:26:11
#> 2 2026-11-26T12:26:11
